name: Temporal Predictive Coding Agent
analogy: Think of it as a trader practicing a lineup game: shown the chart now, plus a stack of possible charts from later, the trader must pick out the one that really came next. Getting good at that game forces the trader to notice the features that actually carry forward in time.

steps.title: Encode each bar into a code
steps.description: An encoder turns each bar's features into a short code. There is no step that rebuilds the bar from the code, so the code is free to keep only what is useful for telling futures apart.
steps.inExample: Each 5-minute MNQ bar is encoded as a code of 32 numbers.

steps.title: Summarize the recent past
steps.description: A small recurrent network reads the codes of the last several bars and forms a running context, which stands for what the agent knows up to now.
steps.inExample: The context at 10:30 summarizes the codes of the previous 24 bars.

steps.title: Gather the true future and decoys
steps.description: For a bar a few steps ahead, the real future code is collected together with a batch of decoy codes taken from other times in the data. The task is to tell the real one from the decoys.
steps.inExample: The real code for the 10:50 bar is placed among 127 decoy codes drawn from other days.

steps.title: Predict and pick the real one
steps.description: The model uses the current context and the actions taken in between to predict what the future code should look like, scores every candidate by how well it matches, and is rewarded when the real one scores highest.
steps.inExample: The model scores all 128 candidates; the real 10:50 code ranks first, so the guess is right.

steps.title: Make the decoys harder
steps.description: Decoys that come from similar market conditions are more instructive than random ones, because telling them apart requires finer features. Training can mix in harder ones as it goes.
steps.inExample: Decoys from other mornings with a similar range and volume are added, so the model must separate subtle differences.

steps.title: Hand the codes to a decision maker
steps.description: The codes feed a policy or value learner trained on rewards, either at the same time or afterward on the frozen codes. Because the codes are forward-predictive, the reward stage can need less reward data.
steps.inExample: A position-sizing policy is trained on the context summaries with profit and cost rewards on walk-forward folds.

useFor.example: Learning forward-predictive codes from years of MNQ bars before any profit label is defined.

useFor.task: Features that work across holding periods
useFor.example: Training for predictions 1, 3 and 6 bars ahead so the codes support both quick and slower trades.

useFor.task: Gauging how predictable the market is right now
useFor.example: Watching the lineup accuracy over time; when it falls, the market has become harder to anticipate.

useFor.task: Starting a data-poor instrument from a rich one
useFor.example: Pretraining on ES and MNQ, then fine-tuning on a thinner contract.
Treating bars where the model cannot pick the real future with confidence as a sign of unusual conditions.

avoidWhen: You need an explicit forecast price or a probability distribution of the next bar; a model that outputs that directly is more useful than a lineup-trained code.
Decoys are too easy, for instance taken from other years with very different price levels; the model then learns the level and not the dynamics.

example.scenario: At 10:30 a trained agent is checked on the lineup task: can it pick the true 10:50 code, four bars ahead, from a batch of 128 candidates?

input.summary: The context built from earlier bars, the actions in between and the 128 candidate future codes.

fields.name: close
fields.meaning: The close of the 10:30 five-minute bar, rounded to a whole point.

fields.name: bars summarized in the context
fields.meaning: How many recent bars the recurrent summary reads.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The typical high-to-low travel of a recent five-minute bar.

fields.name: steps ahead
fields.meaning: How far into the future the candidate codes lie.

fields.name: candidate codes
fields.meaning: The batch the model must choose from.

output.summary: A score for every candidate and the pick.

fields.name: rank of the real code
fields.meaning: Where the true future code landed once the candidates were sorted by score.

fields.name: confidence placed on the real code
fields.meaning: The share of the model's total confidence across all 128 candidates that went to the real one; larger means a clearer pick.

fields.name: lineup accuracy over the last 500 checks
fields.meaning: How often the real code was ranked first in recent checks; a measure of how predictable the market has been.

example.reading: Lineup accuracy is a diagnostic of the representation, not a trading result. Picking at random would win under 1 percent of the time with 128 candidates, so 23 percent is well above chance, though easy decoys inflate it. Whether the codes help a trading policy is a separate test, on walk-forward folds, after costs.
